Claire — great to talk earlier. High level answers up front, then a proposed test protocol and timeline below.

Quick ballpark unit-econ (note: list/starting prices, subject to workload profile/batching/cache):
- Redwood (hosted API, production profile we discussed): ~ $10–12 per 1M tokens baseline (no cache).
- Hyperscaler A (Azure/Managed LLM endpoint): ~ $22–28 per 1M tokens for equivalent model size/throughput in our checks.
- Hyperscaler B (CloudScale AI): ~ $16–20 per 1M tokens.

Important caveats: pricing above collapses infra amortization, model weights, and platform margins into a single per-token number for comparison. Realized unit cost during a given workload depends heavily on batch size, KV/prefix cache hit rate, and the ratio of streaming vs non-streaming tokens. In our experience: enabling moderate batching (4–8) and a 40–60% KV cache hit rate can reduce effective cost per 1M tokens by ~25–40% while keeping p95 latency within acceptable ranges for many UIs.

Proposed 2-week sprint (deliverables at end: raw token logs, cost-per-scenario spreadsheet, p50/p95 latency curves, summary PDF):
1) Baseline single-user (batch=1) latency & quality sweep: 1k sessions, canonical prompt set (we'll provide a 200-prompt golden set), capture p50/p95/p99 latency, token counts.
2) Batch sweep: measure costs and latency at batch sizes [1,4,8,16]; run at target RPS to saturate throughput equal across vendors.
3) Cache-hit matrix: run the same workload with artificial KV/prefix caching at hit rates [0%,25%,50%,75%] to show cost curve and degradation points.
4) Model-variant fallback test: compare large model vs smaller cheaper model with automatic fallback on high load (measure quality delta + cost savings).
5) Streaming vs non-streaming token accounting: measure per-token billing and latency difference for streaming endpoints.

We propose Redwood runs the controlled experiments on our hosted API and provides scripts and data so Vertisys can reproduce the runs against the two hyperscalers. If you prefer, we can also help run the hyperscaler runs under a scoped account to remove variability.

Timeline (two weeks):
- Day 1: finalize canonical prompt set and test harness (we'll share vertisys-bench-protocol.csv).
- Days 2–6: run baseline + batch sweep (parallel across vendors).
- Days 7–10: cache-hit matrix + fallback tests.
- Days 11–13: streaming accounting + QA.
- Day 14: deliverables + walkthrough call.

Cost transparency note: we'll provide token-level cost breakdown (model compute, kernel efficiency, batching overhead) and an apples-to-apples comparison sheet. Expect the delivered per-1M numbers to vary vs the quick ballpark above by ±15% depending on the prompt length distribution and cache effectiveness.

Security / compliance: we can confirm SOC2 and provide audit-log samples; HIPAA arrangements require a DPA + business associate addendum — happy to route to our security team.

Next actions: 1) can you confirm you want us to (A) provide the scripts for you to run against your hyperscaler accounts, or (B) run everything on our side (we'll need scoped admin creds for the hyperscaler accounts)? 2) approve the test plan and the 2-week window starting Monday 3/12.
